mainTopic: Lessons drawn from חנה's prayer and her exchange with עלי
overview: This amud reads חנה's encounter with עלי and her prayer closely, phrase by phrase. From her reply to עלי's mistaken suspicion, the גמרא learns several lessons: a falsely suspected person should explain, someone who wrongly suspects another must appease and bless him, and praying while drunk is compared to עבודה זרה. רבי אלעזר then explains her prayer. She was the first to call God 'צבאות', and a parable about a poor man at a king's feast illustrates her plea. He also reads the doubled 'אם ראה תראה' as a plan to undergo the סוטה process. That plan depends on רבי ישמעאל's reading of the סוטה promise, and רבי עקיבא disagrees, holding that 'דברה תורה כלשון בני אדם'. The three mentions of 'אמתך' hint to נדה, חלה, and lighting the candle. Four views explain 'זרע אנשים'. רבי יהושע בן לוי learns that one may not sit within four אמות of someone praying. רבי אלעזר explains 'אל הנער הזה התפללתי' as חנה's plea to save שמואל, who ruled הלכה in front of עלי. The amud ends with teachings about fasting on שבת and about חנה and אליהו speaking boldly toward Heaven; the proof that ה׳ agreed with אליהו continues on the next amud.

steps.title: An improper act calls for correction
steps.stepSummary: The passage finishes a rule: improper behavior should be corrected.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone does something improper, one must correct that person.
steps.whatsHappening: This line finishes a point begun on the previous amud. It states the rule that someone who sees improper behavior must speak up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The line does not yet explain חנה’s reply. It closes the earlier point before the passage turns to her words.

phrases.english: An improper matter: one must reprimand him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Concludes a discussion that began on the previous amud.

steps.title: The first reading of Hannah’s reply
steps.stepSummary: עולא, or רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא, reads חנה’s words as a direct correction of עלי’s mistaken suspicion.
steps.simpleTranslation: חנה answered, “No, my master.” According to עולא—or רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא—she meant: “In this matter you are not a master, and רוח הקודש is not resting on you, because you suspect me of this.”
steps.whatsHappening: The passage quotes חנה and gives the first explanation of what she meant by “לֹא אֲדוֹנִי.” She tells עלי that his judgment of her was mistaken.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On this reading, “no” denies עלי’s insight into this particular case. His suspicion is the reason חנה says he has not judged it with רוח הקודש.

phrases.english: “Hannah answered and said, ‘No, my master.’”

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר עוּלָּא וְאִיתֵּימָא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא:
phrases.english: Ulla said—and some say Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Hanina, said:

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַרָה לֵיהּ: לֹא אָדוֹן אַתָּה בְּדָבָר זֶה,
phrases.english: She said to him: “You are not a master in this matter,”
“and Divine inspiration does not rest upon you,”
“because you suspect me of this matter.”

steps.triggerLanguage: ״וַתַּעַן חַנָּה וַתֹּאמֶר לֹא אֲדוֹנִי״. אָמַר עוּלָּא וְאִיתֵּימָא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא:
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the completed rule to an explanation of חנה’s reply.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חנה’s “no” points to עלי’s mistaken suspicion in this case.

steps.title: A second reading of Hannah’s reply
steps.stepSummary: Another version reads חנה’s words as a question: how could עלי judge her unfavorably?
steps.simpleTranslation: Others say she asked: “Aren’t you a master? Aren’t שכינה and רוח הקודש with you? Why did you judge me as guilty rather than innocent? Didn’t you know I am a distressed woman?”
steps.whatsHappening: The passage offers a different reading of the same reply. Here חנה questions how עלי could have judged her unfavorably.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first reading said that עלי lacked insight in this case. This reading starts from the expectation that he should have recognized a distressed woman and given her the benefit of the doubt.

phrases.english: Some say she spoke to him this way:
“Are you not a master?”

phrases.aramaic: לָאו אִיכָּא שְׁכִינָה וְרוּחַ הַקּוֹדֶשׁ גַּבָּךְ,
phrases.english: “Are the Divine Presence and Divine inspiration not with you,”

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁדַּנְתַּנִי לְכַף חוֹבָה וְלֹא דַּנְתַּנִי לְכַף זְכוּת?
phrases.english: “that you judged me unfavorably and did not judge me favorably?”

phrases.aramaic: מִי לָא יָדְעַתְּ דְּאִשָּׁה קְשַׁת רוּחַ אָנוֹכִי?!
phrases.english: “Did you not know that I am a woman distressed in spirit?!”

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers another reading of the same words, not a new event.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חנה challenges עלי for judging her unfavorably rather than recognizing her distress.

steps.title: A falsely suspected person should explain
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר learns from חנה’s denial that someone falsely suspected should tell the other person the truth.
steps.simpleTranslation: “I have drunk neither wine nor strong drink.” רבי אלעזר said: From here we learn that someone suspected of something they did not do must make that known.
steps.whatsHappening: The passage turns to חנה’s next words. רבי אלעזר uses her clear denial to teach how a falsely suspected person should respond.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חנה does not leave עלי’s suspicion unanswered. She says plainly that she did not drink; from that response, רבי אלעזר learns that the suspected person should explain their innocence.

phrases.english: “I have drunk neither wine nor strong drink.”
Rabbi Elazar said: From here we learn about someone who is suspected
of something he is not guilty of: he must inform the one who suspects him.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״וְיַיִן וְשֵׁכָר לֹא שָׁתִיתִי״. אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר:
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from readings of חנה’s opening reply to a lesson from her explicit denial.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person falsely suspected should make their innocence known.

steps.title: Prayer while drunk is compared to idol worship
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר states a comparison based on חנה’s phrase “בַּת בְּלִיָּעַל”; the passage will now show its textual basis.
steps.simpleTranslation: “Do not regard your maidservant as a wicked woman.” רבי אלעזר said: From here we learn that one who prays while drunk is as though they worship idols.
steps.whatsHappening: The passage quotes another part of חנה’s reply. רבי אלעזר states a new lesson, setting up the verses that will explain his comparison.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חנה rejects being seen as a “בַּת בְּלִיָּעַל” in the context of suspected drunken prayer. רבי אלעזר links that wording to a drunk person who prays; the next step supplies the link to עבודה זרה.

keyTerms.meaning: a wicked woman; the phrase חנה rejects

phrases.aramaic: ״אַל תִּתֵּן אֶת אֲמָתְךָ לִפְנֵי בַּת בְּלִיָּעַל״.
phrases.english: “Do not regard your maidservant as a wicked woman.”

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: מִכָּאן לְשִׁכּוֹר שֶׁמִּתְפַּלֵּל,
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said: From here we learn that a drunk person who prays
is as though he worships idols.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״אַל תִּתֵּן אֶת אֲמָתְךָ לִפְנֵי בַּת בְּלִיָּעַל״. אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר:
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a separate lesson from another phrase in חנה’s reply.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Praying while drunk is compared to עבודה זרה.

steps.title: The shared word explains the comparison
steps.stepSummary: The passage connects חנה’s “בְּלִיַּעַל” to another verse where the word appears in a case of עבודה זרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here it says “a wicked woman,” and there it says “wicked men have gone out from among you.” Just as the other verse concerns idol worship, so the comparison here is to idol worship.
steps.whatsHappening: The passage now supplies the textual basis for רבי אלעזר’s comparison. It matches the word “בְּלִיַּעַל” in חנה’s words with its use in a verse about עבודה זרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The other verse supplies the connection to עבודה זרה; that connection was not explicit in חנה’s words alone. The conclusion applies that comparison to the drunk person who prays.

keyTerms.meaning: wicked men, in the other verse

phrases.english: It is written here: “as a wicked woman,”

phrases.aramaic: וּכְתִיב הָתָם: ״יָצְאוּ אֲנָשִׁים בְּנֵי בְלִיַּעַל מִקִּרְבֶּךָ״.
phrases.english: and it is written there: “Wicked men have gone out from among you.”

phrases.aramaic: מַה לְּהַלָּן עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה, אַף כָּאן עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה.
phrases.english: Just as there it concerns idol worship, so too here it concerns idol worship.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּתִיב הָכָא: ״לִפְנֵי בַּת בְּלִיַּעַל״, וּכְתִיב הָתָם: ״יָצְאוּ אֲנָשִׁים בְּנֵי בְלִיַּעַל מִקִּרְבֶּךָ״.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the preceding comparison was drawn from the verses.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אלעזר’s comparison of drunken prayer to עבודה זרה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The shared word “בְּלִיַּעַל” in חנה’s reply and in the verse about people leading others toward עבודה זרה.
steps.whatToRemember: The argument rests on a shared word: “בְּלִיַּעַל” connects חנה’s reply to a verse about עבודה זרה.

steps.title: Someone who wrongly suspects another must make peace with him
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר learns from עלי's reply 'go in peace' that one who falsely suspects another must appease him.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And עלי answered and said: Go in peace.' רבי אלעזר said: From here we learn that if someone suspects his friend of something he did not do, he must make peace with him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes עלי's answer to חנה and uses it to teach a rule about how to behave after wrongly suspecting someone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the previous steps, חנה told עלי that his suspicion that she was drunk was wrong. Now we see what עלי did next: he told her 'go in peace.' רבי אלעזר learns that the person who made the mistake must fix the relationship by appeasing the one he hurt.

keyTerms.meaning: Of something that is not true about him
To appease him, to make peace with him

steps.whyThisMatters: This matches the earlier lesson from step 4. There, the person falsely suspected must speak up. Here, the person who suspected must make amends. Together they show both sides of the situation.

phrases.english: "And Eli answered and said: Go in peace"
Rabbi Elazar said:
From here: one who suspects his fellow
of something that is not in him,
that he must appease him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: מִכָּאן לַחוֹשֵׁד אֶת חֲבֵרוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the חנה–עלי exchange. After חנה's denial, the גמרא now draws a lesson from עלי's response.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who wrongly suspects another must appease him.

steps.title: He must also bless the person he suspected
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר adds that besides appeasing, the suspecter must also bless the person. He proves this from עלי's blessing to חנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And not only that, he must also bless him. As it says: 'And may the God of Israel grant your request.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר goes one step further: making peace is not enough, you must also bless the person. He brings the second half of עלי's words as proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'go in peace' taught the duty to appease. The words that follow, 'may God grant your request,' are a blessing. That teaches a second, bigger duty: actively wishing the person well.

keyTerms.meaning: And not only that, but also. Adds a bigger point

steps.whatToRemember: Wrongly suspecting someone creates two duties: appease them (לפייסו) and bless them (לברכו). Both are learned from עלי's words to חנה.

phrases.english: And not only that, but he must bless him.
As it is said:
"And may the God of Israel grant your request."
phrases.notes: שמואל א א:יז, continuation of the same verse

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends step 7's rule with a further obligation, proven from the rest of the verse.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The one who wrongly suspected must also bless the person he suspected.

steps.title: חנה was the first to call God 'צבאות'
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר says that no one in history called God 'צבאות' until חנה did in her vow.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And she made a vow and said: Lord of Hosts.' רבי אלעזר said: From the day God created His world, no person called Him 'צבאות' until חנה came and called Him 'צבאות'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new detail of חנה's prayer: the name of God she used. רבי אלעזר points out that she was the very first person to use it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This opens a new topic. It is no longer about suspicion, but about the words חנה chose. Saying she was 'first' raises a natural question: why did she pick this name? The next step answers that.

keyTerms.meaning: Hosts. A name of God: 'Lord of Hosts'
The Holy One, Blessed be He

phrases.english: "And she vowed a vow and said: Lord of Hosts"
Rabbi Elazar said:

phrases.aramaic: מִיּוֹם שֶׁבָּרָא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא אֶת עוֹלָמוֹ,
phrases.english: From the day that the Holy One, Blessed be He, created His world,
there was no person who called
the Holy One, Blessed be He, "Hosts,"
until Hannah came
and called Him "Hosts."

steps.triggerLanguage: ״וַתִּדֹּר נֶדֶר וַתֹּאמַר ה׳ צְבָאוֹת״, אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from the עלי exchange to another verse in חנה's prayer, still about חנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חנה was the first person in history to address God as 'צבאות'.

steps.title: Why חנה used the name 'צבאות'
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר explains חנה's argument: You created countless hosts, so is one son too hard for You to give?
steps.simpleTranslation: חנה said before God: Master of the world, out of all the countless hosts You created in Your world, is it hard in Your eyes to give me one son?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the meaning behind the name חנה chose. 'צבאות' was not just a title. It was the core of her request.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'צבאות' means God has huge numbers of creations. חנה uses that to argue: compared to so much, one child is tiny. The name itself becomes her reason why God should say yes.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it hard in Your eyes?

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרָה חַנָּה לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא:
phrases.english: Hannah said before the Holy One, Blessed be He:
Master of the world,
of all the hosts upon hosts
that You created in Your world,
is it difficult in Your eyes
to give me one son?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרָה חַנָּה לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא: רִבּוֹנוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the significance of the name introduced in step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חנה called God 'צבאות' to argue that one son is small compared with all His countless creations.

steps.title: The parable begins: a poor man at the king's feast is ignored
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts a parable: a king makes a feast, and a poor man at the door asks for one slice but is ignored.
steps.simpleTranslation: A parable: to what is this similar? To a human king who made a feast for his servants. A poor man came and stood at the door and said to them: Give me one slice! And they paid no attention to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a parable to illustrate חנה's argument. This part only sets the scene. The punch line comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The king is God, the great feast is all of creation, and the poor man is חנה. Being ignored by the servants matches חנה's long years without a child, which led her to turn directly to God.

keyTerms.meaning: Flesh and blood, a human being

phrases.english: A parable: to what is the matter similar?
To a flesh-and-blood king
who made a feast for his servants.

phrases.aramaic: בָּא עָנִי אֶחָד וְעָמַד עַל הַפֶּתַח,
phrases.english: A poor man came and stood at the door,

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָהֶם: תְּנוּ לִי פְּרוּסָה אַחַת!
phrases.english: he said to them: Give me one slice!
And they paid no attention to him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Introduces a parable to illustrate חנה's argument in step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Setup of the parable: a poor man's small request at a great feast is ignored.

steps.title: The poor man pushes in and asks the king directly
steps.stepSummary: The poor man pushes his way to the king and asks: from this whole feast, is one slice too hard to give?
steps.simpleTranslation: He pushed and went in to the king. He said to him: My lord the king, from this whole feast you made, is it hard in your eyes to give me one slice?!
steps.whatsHappening: The parable reaches its point. The poor man's words to the king match חנה's words to God almost exactly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'From this whole feast… one slice' is the same as 'from all the hosts… one son.' The parable shows how strong חנה's argument is. A king with so much loses nothing by giving a tiny bit, and so it is with God.
steps.whatToRemember: חנה called God 'צבאות' to argue: You have endless creations, so one son is a tiny request. The poor man at the king's feast asking for one slice illustrates this.

phrases.english: He pushed and entered before the king.
He said to him: My lord the king,
from this entire feast that you made,
is it difficult in your eyes
to give me one slice?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the parable begun in step 11, matching its punch line to חנה's words in step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The poor man's plea to the king mirrors חנה's plea to God: a small request from one with abundance.

steps.title: חנה says God will see her need
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר reads the repeated word for seeing as חנה’s insistence that God will notice her.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the words “if You will indeed see,” רבי אלעזר says: חנה told God, “If You see my need now, good. If not, You will see it.”
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new reading of חנה’s prayer. Her second “see” sets up the explanation of what she intends to do next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר treats the repeated word as meaningful. The first “see” asks for help now; the second points to another way חנה expects her need to come before God.

phrases.english: “If You will indeed see,”
Rabbi Elazar said:

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרָה חַנָּה לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא:
phrases.english: Hannah said before the Holy One, blessed be He:
Master of the universe,
“If You see” — good,
and if not — “You will see.”

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the parable about asking for one portion, the גמרא turns to another phrase in חנה’s prayer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אלעזר reads חנה’s repeated wording as a promise that her need will be seen.

steps.title: חנה describes how she expects to receive a child
steps.stepSummary: In רבי אלעזר’s reading, חנה proposes to undergo the סוטה process and rely on the verse’s promise to an innocent woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: “I will seclude myself while my husband אלקנה is aware. Then they will give me the סוטה water to drink. You will not make Your תורה false, for it says, ‘She shall be cleared and shall conceive offspring.’”
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what חנה meant by “You will see.” She says she could enter the סוטה process and receive the blessing promised to an innocent woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument depends on the words “she shall conceive offspring.” For this plan to bring חנה a child, those words must promise a child even to a woman who has none.

keyTerms.meaning: the water given in the סוטה process
she shall be cleared and shall conceive offspring

phrases.english: I will go and seclude myself in the presence of Elkana, my husband,

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵיוָן דְּמִסְתַּתַּרְנָא מַשְׁקוּ לִי מֵי סוֹטָה,
phrases.english: and since I secluded myself, they will give me the sota water to drink,
and You will not make Your Torah into a falsehood,
as it says, “She shall be cleared and shall conceive offspring.”

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This spells out the action hinted at by חנה’s second “see.”
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In רבי אלעזר’s reading, חנה relies on the promise attached to the סוטה process.

steps.title: Does that promise give a child to a woman who has none?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי אלעזר’s reading: it works if the verse promises a barren woman a child, but what if it promises only improvements in childbirth?
steps.simpleTranslation: This works according to the view that a barren woman will be granted a child. But according to the view that the promise means easier births, sons instead of daughters, fair children instead of dark children, or tall children instead of short children—what can be said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the verse on which חנה’s plan depends. It sets up a second reading of that verse, which the next lines will identify.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the first reading, the promise could give חנה her first child. On the second, it improves future births for someone who already gives birth; that does not explain how חנה would get a child.

keyTerms.meaning: a woman unable to have children

phrases.english: This works according to the one who says:
If she was barren, she is granted a child—that works well.
But according to the one who says,

phrases.aramaic: אִם הָיְתָה יוֹלֶדֶת בְּצַעַר יוֹלֶדֶת בְּרֶיוַח,
phrases.english: if she used to give birth with pain, she gives birth with ease;
if she bore girls, she bears boys;
if she bore dark children, she bears fair children;
if she bore short children, she bears tall children—
what can be said?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It questions whether the verse cited in חנה’s argument actually promises what she needs.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר’s explanation of חנה’s reliance on “וְנִקְּתָה וְנִזְרְעָה זָרַע.”
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the promise concerns only better births, it does not guarantee a first child to חנה.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל reads the verse as promising a child
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא identifies רבי ישמעאל as the source for the reading that supports חנה’s argument.
steps.simpleTranslation: As taught: “She shall be cleared and shall conceive offspring” teaches that if she was barren, she will be granted a child. These are the words of רבי ישמעאל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to show where the reading just mentioned comes from. רבי ישמעאל says the verse promises a child to a barren woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This reading makes רבי אלעזר’s account of חנה’s plan understandable. The ברייתא will now give the competing reading too.

phrases.english: As it was taught: “She shall be cleared and shall conceive offspring” —
this teaches that if she was barren, she is granted a child,
the words of Rabbi Yishmael.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It identifies the first of the two readings raised in the challenge.
steps.raayaObject: The reading that an innocent barren woman is granted a child.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי ישמעאל’s interpretation in the ברייתא.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא challenges that reading
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא objects that רבי ישמעאל’s reading would give every barren woman a reason to arrange seclusion and then receive a child if innocent.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא said to him: “If so, all barren women will go and seclude themselves, and one who did not act wrongly will be granted a child.”
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא challenges רבי ישמעאל’s interpretation. He points to the result it would produce if the verse guaranteed a child.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge focuses on the promise, not on whether the סוטה process exists. רבי עקיבא argues that a guaranteed child would give barren women a reason to bring about that process.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא: אִם כֵּן,
phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva said to him: If so,
all barren women will go and seclude themselves,
and one who did not act wrongly will be granted a child.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא: אִם כֵּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי עקיבא objects to the reading just attributed to רבי ישמעאל.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ישמעאל’s reading that the verse promises a barren woman a child.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That reading would make seclusion seem like a way for every barren woman to obtain the promised child.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא reads the promise as an improvement in childbirth
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא instead reads the verse as promising better future births, not a first child to a barren woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it teaches that if she used to give birth with pain, she will give birth with ease; if she bore short children, she will bear tall children; if dark children, fair children; if one child, two.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא gives his own reading of the verse. His reading avoids the result he challenged. Steps 19–20 then explain what this means for the doubled wording in חנה's prayer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each example changes the kind of birth or child, rather than promising a first child. That explains why רבי עקיבא disagrees with רבי ישמעאל—and why the גמרא asked how רבי אלעזר’s account of חנה could work according to him.

keyTerms.meaning: instead of one, she gives birth to two

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא gives both readings of the verse. Steps 19–20 explain what רבי עקיבא does with 'אם ראה תראה': the doubling is ordinary speech, so on his view חנה's plan is not derived from it.

phrases.english: Rather, it teaches that if she used to
give birth with pain, she gives birth with ease;
if she bore short children, she bears tall children;
if she bore dark children, she bears fair children;
if she bore one child, she bears two.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי עקיבא replaces the interpretation he challenged with his own.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A different interpretation of the verse’s promise.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The verse guarantees a child even to a woman who was barren.
steps.terutzMaskana: According to רבי עקיבא, the verse promises improvements in future childbirth.

steps.title: What does רבי עקיבא do with the doubled words
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבי עקיבא explains the doubled phrase 'אם ראה תראה', since the סוטה reading that רבי אלעזר drew from it does not work in his view.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבי עקיבא, what is the point of the doubled phrase 'אִם רָאֹה תִרְאֶה' ('if You will surely see')?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the doubled wording in חנה's prayer and asks what it means for רבי עקיבא. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר used the doubled phrase to describe חנה's plan, and that plan relies on רבי ישמעאל's reading of the סוטה verse. רבי עקיבא rejects that reading, so on his view the second 'see' seems to have nothing to teach. The גמרא asks how he explains the repetition.

keyTerms.meaning: 'If You will surely see' — a doubled verb in חנה's prayer
What is / what is the meaning of

phrases.english: What is [the meaning of] 'If You will surely see'?
phrases.notes: Asked from inside רבי עקיבא's view.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבי עקיבא gives his own reading of the סוטה verse, the גמרא asks what he does with the doubled wording that רבי אלעזר expounded.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How רבי עקיבא accounts for the seemingly extra word in 'אם ראה תראה'.

steps.title: The Torah speaks the way people normally speak
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא holds that the doubled language is ordinary human speech, so nothing is learned from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Torah spoke in the normal language of people.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that for רבי עקיבא, the doubled phrase is just a normal way of talking, not a hint to anything.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People often repeat a verb for emphasis, and the Torah sometimes writes the same way. So רבי עקיבא does not have to find a special lesson in the extra word. This answers step 19, and it also resolves step 15's challenge: רבי אלעזר's reading follows רבי ישמעאל, while רבי עקיבא draws no lesson from the doubling.

keyTerms.meaning: The Torah spoke in human language; a repeated word does not always teach something new

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אלעזר's lesson from the doubled phrase fits רבי ישמעאל's reading of the סוטה promise. According to רבי עקיבא, 'דברה תורה כלשון בני אדם', so the repetition is just normal speech.
steps.confusionAlert: This famous phrase is usually linked to רבי ישמעאל elsewhere in ש״ס. Here, it is used to explain רבי עקיבא's view. Do not mix up who says it in this סוגיא.

phrases.english: The Torah spoke in the language of people.
phrases.notes: So the doubling is ordinary style, and no lesson is drawn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The doubled verb is normal human speech, so רבי עקיבא draws no lesson from it.

steps.title: חנה calls herself 'Your maidservant' three times
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the three places in the verse where חנה calls herself 'אמתך', setting up the next explanation.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'The suffering of Your maidservant.' 'Do not forget Your maidservant.' 'And You will give Your maidservant.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. It lists three phrases from חנה's prayer that each use the word 'maidservant'. This is a setup line for רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One mention of 'Your maidservant' would have been enough, so saying it three times stands out. The גמרא lines up all three so we notice the repetition before hearing the reason for it.

phrases.english: 'The affliction of Your maidservant.'
'Do not forget Your maidservant.'
'And You will give Your maidservant.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the doubled-verb debate to a different detail in the same verse.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The verse uses 'אמתך' three times. This is the textual base for the next teaching.

steps.title: The three mentions hint to three מצוות for women
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא explains that the three mentions of 'אמתך' hint to נדה, חלה, and lighting the candles, which חנה never violated.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said: Why are these three 'maidservants' here? חנה said before the Holy One, Blessed be He: 'Master of the world, You created three tests that can bring death to a woman.' Some say: 'three things that bring on death.' They are נדה, חלה, and lighting the candle. 'Have I ever broken even one of them?'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא gives the reason for the three mentions. חנה was pointing to three special women's מצוות and saying she kept all of them, so she deserves a child.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אמה (maidservant) sounds like מיתה (death), so the three mentions hint to three areas where a woman can be judged severely. חנה uses her faithfulness in these three מצוות as the basis of her request. The two versions (בדקי or דבקי) differ only in one word: 'tests' versus 'things that cling to / speed up' death.

keyTerms.meaning: Tests that can lead to death (where a woman is judged)
Things that cling to / bring on death (alternate version)
And some say (introduces a different version)
The laws of family purity, separating dough, and lighting Shabbos candles

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a well-known source linking נדה, חלה, and הדלקת נר specifically to women. It echoes the משנה in שבת (ב:ו) about women being judged on these three מצוות.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Ḥanina said:
Why these three 'maidservants'?

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרָה חַנָּה לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא:
phrases.english: Hannah said before the Holy One, Blessed be He:
Master of the Universe,
You created three tests of death in a woman,
and some say: three accelerants of death.

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵלּוּ הֵן: נִדָּה, וְחַלָּה וְהַדְלָקַת הַנֵּר.
phrases.english: And they are: menstrual laws, ḥalla, and lighting the lamp.
Have I ever violated even one of them?!
phrases.notes: So she deserves to be answered.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא: שָׁלֹשׁ אֲמָתוֹת הַלָּלוּ לָמָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the threefold repetition quoted in step 21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The three mentions of אמתך hint to נדה, חלה, and הדלקת הנר. חנה claims she kept all three, so she deserves a child.

steps.title: Quoting 'offspring of men' to set up the next teaching
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next phrase of חנה's prayer, 'זרע אנשים', so it can explain it next.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And You will give Your maidservant an offspring of men.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next words of the verse. This is a setup line: steps 24–29 explain what 'זרע אנשים' means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חנה did not just ask for a child; she asked for 'זרע אנשים', a 'seed of men'. That unusual wording invites a question about what kind of child she meant, and the גמרא will address it next.

keyTerms.meaning: Offspring of men; a child of a special kind, explained next

phrases.english: 'And You will give Your maidservant an offspring of men.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next phrase of the same verse after finishing the 'three maidservants' teaching.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Quotes 'זרע אנשים' as the base text for the next teaching.

steps.title: What does 'an offspring of men' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what חנה meant when she asked for 'זרע אנשים'.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the meaning of 'an offspring of men'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the words 'זרע אנשים' in חנה's prayer mean. This sets up several different answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every child is born from people, so the words 'of men' seem to add nothing. The גמרא assumes the extra word must be teaching something about the kind of son חנה wanted.

keyTerms.meaning: An offspring of men; חנה's request in שמואל א א:יא

phrases.english: What is 'an offspring of men'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of the phrase quoted in step 23.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What kind of child חנה was asking for with the words 'זרע אנשים'.

steps.title: רב: an outstanding man among men
steps.stepSummary: רב explains that חנה asked for a son who would stand out among men.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: a man among men.
steps.whatsHappening: רב gives the first answer: חנה wanted a son who would be a leader and stand out from everyone else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב reads 'אנשים' as 'real men', meaning important people. So the phrase means a son who is great even among great people.

keyTerms.meaning: A man among men; an outstanding person

phrases.english: Rav said:
A man among men.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to the question in step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A son who would be exceptional among men.

steps.title: שמואל: a son who will anoint two men as kings
steps.stepSummary: שמואל explains that חנה asked for a son who would anoint two kings, שאול and דוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל said: an offspring who will anoint two men. And who are they? שאול and דוד.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives a second answer: 'אנשים' (plural, at least two) hints at the two kings her son would anoint.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל reads the plural 'men' as a number: two specific men. History shows that שמואל הנביא anointed שאול and later דוד, so חנה's prayer was for a son with that role.

keyTerms.meaning: Anoints (with oil, to make someone king)

steps.confusionAlert: There are two people called שמואל here. The one giving this explanation is the אמורא שמואל. The child חנה is praying for is שמואל הנביא.

phrases.english: And Shmuel said:
An offspring who anoints two men,
And who are they? Saul and David.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר: זֶרַע שֶׁמּוֹשֵׁחַ שְׁנֵי אֲנָשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, different answer to step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A son who would anoint two kings, שאול and דוד.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: a son equal to משה and אהרן
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains that חנה asked for a son as great as משה and אהרן together, and he brings a פסוק as proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: an offspring who is equal to two men. And who are they? משה and אהרן. As it says: 'משה and אהרן among His כהנים, and שמואל among those who call His name.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a third answer: the 'two men' are משה and אהרן, and her son would be equal to both of them. He proves it from a פסוק in תהלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like שמואל, רבי יוחנן reads 'אנשים' as two people, but for him they are people her son would match, not people he would anoint. The פסוק in תהלים צט lists שמואל alongside משה and אהרן, which shows that he is weighed equal to them.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is said (introduces a פסוק)
Among those who call His name

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
An offspring who is equal to two men,
And who are they? Moses and Aaron.
As it is stated:
"Moses and Aaron among His priests,
and Samuel among those who call His name."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: זֶרַע שֶׁשָּׁקוּל כִּשְׁנֵי אֲנָשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third answer to step 24, this time with a supporting פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A son as great as משה and אהרן combined, proven from תהלים צט:ו.

steps.title: The רבנן: a son who blends in among people
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן explain that חנה asked for a son who would not stand out in his looks or traits.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן say: 'an offspring of men' means an offspring who is blended in among men.
steps.whatsHappening: The רבנן give a fourth answer: חנה wanted a normal-looking son who would fit in with everyone and not draw attention.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is close to the opposite of רב. Instead of standing out, the son should be 'swallowed up' among ordinary people. Such a person does not attract an עין הרע or ridicule.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say:
"An offspring of men":
An offspring who is blended in among men.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּנַן אָמְרִי: ״זֶרַע אֲנָשִׁים״ — זֶרַע שֶׁמּוּבְלָע בֵּין אֲנָשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The fourth and last answer to step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A son who would be inconspicuous among people.

steps.title: רב דימי spells out what 'blending in' means
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי lists the extremes the son should avoid: not too tall or short, thin or fat, pale or red, smart or foolish.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב דימי came from ארץ ישראל, he said: not too tall and not too short, not too thin and not too fat, not too white and not too red, not too smart and not too foolish.
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי explains the רבנן's view in detail by listing the pairs of extremes that make a person stand out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every pair names two opposite extremes, and the goal is the middle of each one. Even being 'too smart' counts as standing out, so 'blending in' covers looks and intelligence alike.

keyTerms.meaning: When he came (usually from ארץ ישראל to בבל)

steps.whatToRemember: There are four views on 'זרע אנשים': רב says an outstanding man, שמואל says one who anoints שאול and דוד, רבי יוחנן says one equal to משה and אהרן, and the רבנן say one who blends in (as רב דימי explains).

phrases.english: When Rav Dimi came, he said:
Neither tall nor short,
neither small nor fat,
neither white nor red,
neither wise nor foolish.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands on the רבנן's view from step 28.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Blending in means being in the middle of every physical and mental extreme.

steps.title: Do not sit within four אמות of someone davening
steps.stepSummary: From חנה's words 'who stood with you here', רבי יהושע בן לוי learns that one may not sit within four אמות of a person davening.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'I am the woman who stood with you here.' רבי יהושע בן לוי said: from here we learn that it is forbidden to sit within four אמות of תפלה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next פסוק in the story, and רבי יהושע בן לוי learns a practical הלכה from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חנה says that עלי was standing with her while she davened. That shows עלי did not sit while near someone praying, so it is forbidden to sit within four אמות of someone davening.

keyTerms.meaning: Four cubits; the personal space around a person

steps.whyThisMatters: This is an actual הלכה about how to behave near someone saying שמונה עשרה. It is brought in שולחן ערוך.

phrases.english: "I am the woman who stood
with you here,"
Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
From here, that it is forbidden to sit
within four cubits of prayer.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי: מִכָּאן שֶׁאָסוּר לֵישֵׁב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next פסוק in חנה's story and derives a הלכה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: It is forbidden to sit within four אמות of someone davening.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: שמואל ruled in front of his teacher
steps.stepSummary: On 'for this boy I prayed', רבי אלעזר says that שמואל gave a הלכה ruling in front of his teacher עלי.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'For this boy I prayed.' רבי אלעזר said: שמואל was one who ruled הלכה in front of his teacher.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next פסוק, and רבי אלעזר explains the background: young שמואל had ruled on a הלכה in front of עלי, his teacher. That is a serious offense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חנה stresses 'this boy' because the boy was in danger. Ruling in front of one's teacher can carry the punishment of death by the hands of Heaven. The גמרא will now prove that this event happened.

phrases.english: "For this youth I prayed."
Rabbi Elazar said:
Samuel was one who ruled halakha
in front of his teacher.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: שְׁמוּאֵל מוֹרֵה הֲלָכָה לִפְנֵי רַבּוֹ הָיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next פסוק and gives a new explanation.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שמואל ruled on a הלכה in front of his teacher עלי, which put him in danger.

steps.title: The verse about slaughtering the bull
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר brings a פסוק to prove his claim: they slaughtered the bull and brought the boy to עלי.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'And they slaughtered the bull, and they brought the boy to עלי.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר quotes the פסוק that he says hints at the story of שמואל ruling in front of עלי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof depends on the order of events in the פסוק: first the slaughter, then the boy is brought to עלי. That order suggests the slaughter caused the boy to be brought, which the next line will point out.

phrases.english: As it is stated:
"And they slaughtered the bull,
and they brought the youth to Eli."

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וַיִּשְׁחֲטוּ אֶת הַפָּר וַיָּבִיאוּ אֶת הַנַּעַר אֶל עֵלִי״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the פסוק that supports רבי אלעזר's claim in step 31.
steps.raayaObject: That שמואל ruled הלכה in front of עלי.

steps.title: Why would slaughtering the bull lead to bringing the boy?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out how strange the פסוק is: why should the slaughter cause them to bring the boy to עלי?
steps.simpleTranslation: Because 'they slaughtered the bull', they brought the boy to עלי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a pointed question about the פסוק: what does slaughtering the bull have to do with bringing the boy to עלי? This sets up the story the גמרא will tell next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is not an attack on רבי אלעזר. It shows that the פסוק makes sense only if something happened during the slaughter that involved the boy. That hidden event is שמואל's ruling, which the גמרא is about to describe.

phrases.english: Because "they slaughtered the bull"
they brought the youth to Eli?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם דְּ״וַיִּשְׁחֲטוּ אֶת הַפָּר״ הֵבִיאוּ הַנַּעַר אֶל עֵלִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Points out the oddity in the פסוק from step 32 to show that it hides an event.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What connection between the slaughter and bringing the boy to עלי explains the פסוק.

steps.title: What really happened: שמואל says a non-priest may slaughter
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא retells the story. עלי asked for a כהן to slaughter, and שמואל said a זר may do it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, עלי told them to call a כהן to come and slaughter. שמואל saw them searching for a כהן and asked why they needed one, since slaughter by a non-priest is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 33 by filling in the missing story between the slaughter and bringing the boy to עלי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק seemed odd because slaughtering an animal is no reason to bring a child to עלי. The answer is that the slaughter caused a halachic discussion: people searched for a כהן, and שמואל told them it was not necessary. That ruling is why they brought him to עלי.

phrases.english: Rather,
Eli said to them:
Call a priest, let him come and slaughter.
Shmuel saw them
that they were searching for a priest to slaughter,
he said to them:

phrases.aramaic: לְמָה לְכוּ לְאַהְדּוֹרֵי בָּתַר כֹּהֵן לְמִישְׁחַט?
phrases.english: Why do you need to search for a priest to slaughter?
Slaughter by a non-priest is valid!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the oddness of the פסוק raised in Step 33
steps.terutzResolutionType: Supplying the missing story behind the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The slaughter seems to have no connection to bringing the boy to עלי
steps.terutzMaskana: The slaughter led to שמואל's halachic ruling, and that ruling is why he was brought to עלי

steps.title: עלי asks שמואל for his source
steps.stepSummary: They brought שמואל to עלי, who asked him how he knew this.
steps.simpleTranslation: They brought him before עלי. עלי said to him: From where do you know this?
steps.whatsHappening: עלי asks the young שמואל to show where his ruling comes from. This sets up שמואל's proof in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line explains the פסוק 'and they brought the boy to עלי.' עלי does not reject the ruling. He asks for its source.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do you know this?

phrases.english: They brought him before Eli.
He said to him: From where do you know this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of שמואל's ruling
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source showing that a זר may slaughter

steps.title: שמואל proves his ruling from the פסוק
steps.stepSummary: The Torah says 'the כהנים shall bring near' only from receiving the blood onward. So slaughter by a זר is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does it say 'and the כהן shall slaughter'? It says 'and the כהנים shall bring near.' The כהנים‎' מצוה starts from receiving the blood. From here we learn that slaughter by a זר is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל answers עלי with a proof from how the Torah words the steps of a קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק names the כהנים only when it reaches קבלה, the receiving of the blood. The Torah does not mention them for the שחיטה. So the work reserved for כהנים begins with קבלה, and a זר may do the שחיטה.

keyTerms.meaning: Receiving the blood in a vessel

phrases.english: He said to him:
Is it written "and the priest shall slaughter"?!
"And the priests shall bring near" is written,
from receiving the blood onward is the מצוה of the priesthood;
from here we learn that slaughter is valid by a non-priest.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers עלי's question with a פסוק
steps.raayaSupportSource: The פסוק 'והקריבו הכהנים', which names the כהנים only from קבלה onward
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a real הלכה in קדשים: a זר may perform שחיטה of a קרבן.

steps.title: Correct, but ruling before one's teacher deserves death
steps.stepSummary: עלי agrees with the ruling but says that whoever rules הלכה before his teacher is liable to מיתה.
steps.simpleTranslation: You are right. However, you ruled הלכה in front of your teacher, and anyone who rules הלכה in front of his teacher is liable to death.
steps.whatsHappening: עלי accepts שמואל's ruling, then raises a separate problem: שמואל ruled in his teacher's presence. This is the point רבי אלעזר made in Step 31.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem is not that the ruling was wrong. It was correct. The wrong was the disrespect of deciding הלכה while one's רבי is present. That alone makes him liable to מיתה בידי שמים.

keyTerms.meaning: Ruling on a matter of הלכה

steps.confusionAlert: עלי is not disputing the הלכה. He agrees that a זר may slaughter. The only problem is ruling in front of one's teacher.
steps.whyThisMatters: This story is the source for the serious prohibition against paskening הלכה in front of one's רבי.

phrases.english: He said to him:
You are speaking well,

phrases.aramaic: מִיהוּ מוֹרֶה הֲלָכָה בִּפְנֵי רַבָּךְ אַתְּ,
phrases.english: however, you are ruling halacha in front of your teacher,
and anyone who rules halacha in front of his teacher
is liable to death.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵימָר שַׁפִּיר קָא אָמְרַתְּ, מִיהוּ מוֹרֶה הֲלָכָה בִּפְנֵי רַבָּךְ אַתְּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the proof but raises a separate wrongdoing
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Ruling הלכה in front of one's teacher makes one liable to מיתה, even if the ruling is correct

steps.title: חנה pleads for her son: 'For this boy I prayed'
steps.stepSummary: חנה cried out that she was the woman who prayed there. עלי offered to pray for a greater son. She answered that she prayed for this boy.
steps.simpleTranslation: חנה came and cried before him: 'I am the woman who stood with you here.' He said: Let me punish him, and I will pray that you be given someone greater. She said: 'For this boy I prayed.'
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends, and we now see how the words 'אל הנער הזה התפללתי' fit the story, as Step 31 said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חנה reminds עלי that this child came from her תפילה. עלי offers a greater replacement, but she insists on this particular child. Read this way, the פסוק becomes a plea to save שמואל's life.
steps.whatToRemember: The words 'For this boy I prayed' were חנה's plea to save שמואל after he ruled in front of עלי. This completes רבי אלעזר's reading from Step 31.

phrases.english: Chana came and was crying out before him:
"I am the woman who stood with you here, etc."
He said to her: Let me punish him,
and I will pray for mercy,
and He will give you one greater than him.
She said to him: "For this boy I prayed."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the story and ties it back to the פסוק from Step 31
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The פסוק 'אל הנער הזה התפללתי' was חנה's plea to save שמואל's life

steps.title: חנה's argument: nothing in a woman's body was made for no reason
steps.stepSummary: 'על לבה' means 'about matters of her heart.' חנה argued that her breasts must have a purpose, so ה׳ should give her a son.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And חנה spoke on her heart.' רבי אלעזר in the name of רבי יוסי בן זמרא: about matters of her heart. She said: Master of the world, You made nothing in a woman for no reason. Eyes see, ears hear, a nose smells, a mouth speaks, hands work, feet walk, breasts nurse. Why did You put these breasts on my heart, if not to nurse? Give me a son, and I will nurse with them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to חנה's תפילה and explains a new phrase from the פסוקים, 'על לבה.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The odd word 'על' ('on' her heart) is read as 'about matters of her heart,' meaning the breasts that lie on her heart. חנה's argument goes from the general to the specific. Every body part has a purpose, so her breasts must be meant for nursing. Therefore ה׳ should give her a son.

phrases.english: "And Chana was speaking on her heart."

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן זִמְרָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said in the name of Rabbi Yosei ben Zimra:
About matters of her heart.
She said before Him: Master of the world,
of everything You created in a woman,
You did not create one thing for no purpose:
eyes to see, and ears to hear,
a nose to smell, a mouth to speak,
hands to do work with them,

phrases.aramaic: רַגְלַיִם לְהַלֵּךְ בָּהֶן, דַּדִּים לְהָנִיק בָּהֶן.
phrases.english: feet to walk with them, breasts to nurse with them.

phrases.aramaic: דַּדִּים הַלָּלוּ שֶׁנָּתַתָּ עַל לִבִּי לָמָּה?
phrases.english: These breasts that You placed on my heart, what are they for?
Is it not to nurse with them?!
Give me a son, and I will nurse with them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to explaining another phrase in חנה's תפילה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'על לבה' means חנה prayed about the purpose of her breasts, arguing that they show she was meant to have a son

steps.title: Fasting on שבת: a harsh decree is torn up, but there is a price
steps.stepSummary: Whoever fasts on שבת has a seventy-year decree torn up, but he is then punished for not keeping עונג שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר also said in the name of רבי יוסי בן זמרא: Whoever fasts on שבת has his seventy-year sentence torn up. Even so, he is later punished for neglecting the מצוה of enjoying שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: Because the same chain of rabbis was just quoted, the גמרא adds another teaching from them on a different topic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The statement has two parts. Fasting on שבת is very powerful and can cancel a bad decree. But it goes against the מצוה of עונג שבת, so the person must still answer for that.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not a recommendation to fast on שבת. The second half warns that the person is still punished for neglecting עונג שבת.
steps.whatToRemember: Fasting on שבת is powerful enough to tear up a decree, yet it still carries a cost for neglecting עונג שבת.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן זִמְרָא:
phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar said in the name of Rabbi Yosei ben Zimra:
Anyone who sits in a fast on Shabbat,

phrases.aramaic: קוֹרְעִים לוֹ גְּזַר דִּינוֹ שֶׁל שִׁבְעִים שָׁנָה.
phrases.english: they tear up for him his sentence of seventy years.

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל פִּי כֵן חוֹזְרִין וְנִפְרָעִין מִמֶּנּוּ
phrases.english: And even so, they then come back and punish him
for the law of enjoying Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן זִמְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: An unrelated teaching added because it comes from the same chain of rabbis
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Fasting on שבת tears up a seventy-year decree, but the person is still punished for neglecting עונג שבת

steps.title: What can someone do to fix fasting on שבת?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how a person who fasted on שבת can repair the damage of not keeping עונג שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is his fix?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short follow-up question about the person from the last step. It is setting up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 40 said that fasting on שבת can tear up a bad decree, but the person is punished for losing עונג שבת. So the person seems stuck. The גמרא wants to know if there is a way out.

phrases.english: What is his remedy?
phrases.notes: Refers to the person who fasted on שבת and is now punished for missing עונג שבת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a practical fix to the problem raised in Step 40.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How can someone who fasted on שבת avoid the punishment for losing עונג שבת?

steps.title: Fast again to make up for the fast
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers that the person should fast another day, on a weekday, to make up for fasting on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: He should sit in a fast to make up for the fast.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק gives the fix: fast again on a regular weekday.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The weekday fast acts as a תשובה for the שבת fast. The person keeps the good result of the first fast, because the decree is torn up. The second fast takes care of the sin of losing עונג שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: He should sit (here: he should observe a fast)
A fast because of a bad dream (the פוסקים apply this passage to such a fast; the text itself just says a fast)

steps.whatToRemember: Fasting on שבת can tear up a bad decree, but the person must fast again on a weekday to make up for losing עונג שבת.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
He should sit in a fast for the fast.
phrases.notes: In other words, he fasts again on a weekday to atone for fasting on שבת.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק לִיתֵּיב תַּעֲנִיתָא לְתַעֲנִיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 41.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He should do another fast on a weekday to atone for fasting on שבת.

steps.title: חנה spoke boldly toward Heaven
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר says חנה spoke boldly to ה׳. He learns this from the verse that says she prayed 'עַל ה׳' (onto ה׳) instead of 'אֶל ה׳' (to ה׳).
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אלעזר said: חנה threw words up toward Heaven. As it says, 'And she prayed onto ה׳.' This teaches that she threw words up toward Heaven.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the story of חנה and brings another teaching about her prayer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The usual way to say it would be 'she prayed אֶל ה׳' (to ה׳). The verse says 'עַל ה׳', which can mean 'against' or 'upon' ה׳. From this unusual wording, רבי אלעזר learns that she spoke to ה׳ in a bold, demanding way.

keyTerms.meaning: She threw words / spoke boldly and harshly
Toward Heaven, meaning toward ה׳ (said respectfully)
And she prayed onto ה׳‎ (שמואל א א:י)

steps.confusionAlert: 'כְּלַפֵּי מַעְלָה' (toward Above) is a respectful way of saying 'toward ה׳.' The word הֵטִיחָה ('hurled') describes bold, demanding words, not a physical act. It describes how bold her prayer was, like her argument in Step 39.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar said:
Chana hurled words toward Above.
As it says: 'And she prayed onto ה׳,'
phrases.notes: The verse says 'עַל' and not the usual 'אֶל'.

phrases.english: This teaches that she hurled words toward Above.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר חַנָּה הֵטִיחָה דְּבָרִים כְּלַפֵּי מַעְלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back from the side topic of fasting on שבת to the story of חנה's prayer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חנה spoke boldly to ה׳, as shown by the wording 'עַל ה׳'.

steps.title: אליהו also spoke boldly toward Heaven
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר says אליהו also spoke boldly to ה׳. On הר הכרמל, אליהו said, 'You turned their hearts backward,' which suggests that ה׳ caused ישראל to sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אלעזר said: אליהו threw words up toward Heaven. As it says, 'And You turned their heart backward.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר gives a second example of someone who spoke boldly to ה׳. This time it is אליהו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In his prayer on הר הכרמל, אליהו said that ה׳ was the one who turned ישראל's hearts away. That sounds like blaming ה׳ for their sin, so רבי אלעזר calls it speaking boldly toward Heaven.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar said:
Eliyahu hurled words toward Above,
As it says: 'And You turned their heart backward.'
phrases.notes: מלכים א יח:לז. אליהו says that ה׳ caused ישראל to turn away.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אֵלִיָּהוּ הֵטִיחַ דְּבָרִים כְּלַפֵּי מַעְלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another teaching from the same רבי אלעזר, using the same idea of speaking boldly toward Heaven.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אליהו spoke boldly to ה׳ when he said, 'You turned their heart backward.'

steps.title: Where do we see ה׳ agreed with אליהו?
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמואל בר רבי יצחק asks where we learn that ה׳ later admitted אליהו was right.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמואל בר רבי יצחק said: From where do we know that הקדוש ברוך הוא later agreed with אליהו?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question is asked about אליהו's bold words. This step is a setup; the answer comes in the next part of the גמרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This question changes the picture of Step 44. אליהו's bold words were not simply wrong, because ה׳ Himself later agreed with him. The גמרא now looks for the verse that shows this.

keyTerms.meaning: The Holy One, Blessed is He
He admitted to him / agreed with him

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר רַבִּי יִצְחָק:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shmuel bar Rabbi Yitzchak said:
From where do we know that the Holy One, Blessed is He, came back
and admitted to Eliyahu,
phrases.notes: The answer (a verse) continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר רַבִּי יִצְחָק מִנַּיִן שֶׁחָזַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא וְהוֹדָה לוֹ לְאֵלִיָּהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on Step 44 by asking for proof that ה׳ agreed with אליהו's bold words.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which verse shows that ה׳ later agreed with אליהו's claim?
